content:
# The 54 Best AI Tools in 2026, Grouped by What You Do

This is a working directory rather than a leaderboard. Fifty-four tools across writing, images, productivity, coding, audio and video, chosen because each one does a specific job well enough that people keep using it past the trial month.

Every entry below carries the same four facts: what the tool is best at, the one thing it does noticeably better than its neighbours, the catch that shows up after a few weeks, and what it costs. Pricing and feature notes come from the vendor, so verify on the current pricing page before you commit — plan tiers change faster than any guide can track.

## Table of Contents
- [Writing Tools](#writing-tools)
- [Image Generation](#image-generation)
- [Productivity](#productivity)
- [Coding Assistants](#coding-assistants)
- [Audio & Music](#audio--music)
- [Video Editing](#video-editing)
- [More Tools Worth Knowing](#more-tools-worth-knowing)

---

## Writing Tools

These are assistants, not authors. They shorten the distance between a draft and a finished draft; they do not decide what to say. The cheap ones are good enough for most people, and the expensive ones earn their keep only when a whole team has to sound the same.

### 1. [[link:/tools/6|ChatGPT]]
ChatGPT is OpenAI's general-purpose conversational assistant used for writing, analysis, coding, brainstorming, and everyday questions.
- **Best for:** Drafting Documents, Code Help, File Analysis
- **Standout:** Handles text, images, files, and voice in one conversational interface
- Access may require a VPN in some regions
- **Pricing:** Freemium

### 2. [[link:/tools/18|Jasper]]
Jasper is an enterprise-grade AI writing platform for marketing teams.
- **Best for:** Brand Campaigns, Long-Form SEO, Team Workflows
- **Standout:** Brand Voice training keeps large teams aligned on tone and terminology
- **Watch out for:** Paid-only pricing with per-seat costs is expensive for individuals
- **Pricing:** Paid

### 3. [[link:/tools/20|Claude]]
Claude is Anthropic's assistant built for long documents, writing and analysis.
- **Best for:** Long Document Review, Structured Writing, Live Artifacts
- **Standout:** Large context window handles lengthy documents without splitting them
- Regional access may need a VPN in places
- **Pricing:** Freemium

### 4. [[link:/tools/21|Gemini]]
Gemini is Google's multimodal assistant, integrated with Search, Workspace, and Android.
- **Best for:** Workspace Drafting, Research Help, File Understanding
- **Standout:** Deep Workspace integration puts assistance inside Gmail, Docs, and Sheets
- **Watch out for:** Availability varies by region and some features require supported countries
- **Pricing:** Freemium

### 5. [[link:/tools/22|Writesonic]]
Writesonic is a content marketing platform for AI article drafting and SEO-optimized copy.
- **Best for:** SEO Articles, Brand-Voice Chat, Publishing Handoff
- **Standout:** Publishing integrations move drafts toward release without retyping
- Some regions need a VPN to reach it
- **Pricing:** Freemium

### 6. [[link:/tools/23|Rytr]]
The most affordable AI writing tool trusted by 10M+ creators worldwide.
- **Best for:** SEO Blog Posts, Email Campaigns, Social Media Content
- **Standout:** Unbeatable value — $9/month with 40+ templates and unlimited words on premium plan
- **Watch out for:** Long-form editor lacks the advanced customization of enterprise tools like Jasper
- **Pricing:** Freemium

### 7. [[link:/tools/24|QuillBot]]
QuillBot is a writing tool built around paraphrasing, with grammar checking, summarization, and citation generation included.
- **Best for:** Paraphrasing Text, Summaries, Citations
- **Standout:** Multiple paraphrase modes let users adjust tone without rewriting by hand
- Availability varies by country; a VPN may be required
- **Pricing:** Freemium

### 8. [[link:/tools/57|SurferSEO]]
SurferSEO is a content optimization tool that scores drafts against pages currently ranking for target keywords.
- **Best for:** Content Scoring, Structure Guidance, Internal Linking
- **Standout:** Real-time scoring gives concrete targets while the draft is being written
- Where it is blocked, a VPN is the usual workaround
- **Pricing:** Paid

### 9. [[link:/tools/58|Frase]]
Frase is a content research and writing tool for SEO workflows.
- **Best for:** Content Briefs, Gap Analysis, SEO Drafting
- **Standout:** Combines SERP research, briefing and drafting in one workflow
- **Watch out for:** Paid-only pricing puts it out of reach for occasional writers
- **Pricing:** Paid

### 10. [[link:/tools/59|MarketMuse]]
MarketMuse is a content strategy platform that uses topic models to plan and prioritize content.
- **Best for:** Content Clusters, Page Audits, Priority Planning
- **Standout:** Strategy-level planning goes beyond individual article writing
- **Watch out for:** Paid-only and priced for teams with content budgets
- **Pricing:** Paid

---

## Image Generation

Generation quality has converged far more than the interfaces have. What separates these is control — how much you can steer a result, whether it runs locally, and whether the output is licensed for commercial use.

### 11. [[link:/tools/1|Midjourney]]
Midjourney is a leading AI image generator that turns text prompts into stylized, high-quality visuals.
- **Best for:** Concept Art, Illustration Styles, Social Visuals
- **Standout:** Strong style consistency across a set of generated images
- **Pricing:** Freemium

### 12. [[link:/tools/2|DALL-E 3]]
DALL-E 3 is OpenAI's text-to-image model, available through ChatGPT Plus, the API, and Bing Image Creator.
- **Best for:** Illustrated Concepts, Text in Images, Prompt Experimentation
- **Standout:** Interprets long, detailed prompts and renders legible text better than rivals
- **Watch out for:** Subscription required for regular use, with free access limited to occasional trials
- **Pricing:** Freemium

### 13. [[link:/tools/3|Stable Diffusion]]
Stable Diffusion is the open-weights image model behind much of the generative art ecosystem.
- **Best for:** Custom Models, Local Generation, Precise Sampling
- **Standout:** Full control over sampling, styles and model fine-tuning
- **Watch out for:** Local setup is technical and needs a capable GPU
- **Pricing:** Open Source

### 14. [[link:/tools/294|Canva AI]]
Canva AI brings AI-powered design features into the Canva platform.
- **Best for:** Social Graphics, Text Effects, Template Customization
- **Standout:** AI features integrated directly into the Canva editor
- **Watch out for:** Premium templates and assets require a paid plan
- **Pricing:** Freemium

### 15. [[link:/tools/19|Adobe Firefly]]
Adobe Firefly is Adobe's family of generative image and video models, wired directly into Photoshop, Illustrator and Express.
- **Best for:** Generative Fill, Text-to-Image, Commercial Assets
- **Standout:** Integrated into Photoshop, Illustrator and Express, not a separate tool
- **Watch out for:** Full use inside Creative Cloud apps requires a paid subscription
- **Pricing:** Freemium

### 16. [[link:/tools/66|Spline AI]]
Spline AI is a 3D design tool with prompt-based generation, materials, and animation features.
- **Best for:** Web 3D Scenes, Social Content, Product Visuals
- **Standout:** Prompt-based 3D generation lowers the barrier for beginners
- **Watch out for:** Complex scenes may need manual tuning after generation
- **Pricing:** Freemium

### 17. [[link:/tools/67|Meshy]]
Meshy is an AI tool that generates 3D models from text prompts or reference images.
- **Best for:** Game Asset Creation, 3D Print Models, Rigging Automation
- **Standout:** Supports both text and image inputs for flexible 3D generation
- **Pricing:** Freemium

### 18. [[link:/tools/68|Leonardo AI]]
Leonardo AI is an image generation platform aimed at game artists, product designers, and other creative professionals.
- **Best for:** Game Assets, Product Concepts, Image Editing
- **Standout:** Fine-tuned models target specific styles like game art and product shots
- **Pricing:** Freemium

### 19. [[link:/tools/75|Lexica]]
Lexica is a search engine and gallery for AI-generated images, built around a large index of Stable Diffusion prompts and results.
- **Best for:** Prompt Research, Image Generation, API Integration
- **Standout:** Searchable prompt gallery makes it easy to learn effective phrasing patterns
- **Pricing:** Freemium

### 20. [[link:/tools/76|Playground AI]]
Playground AI is a browser-based image editor combining AI generation, inpainting, filters, and canvas layout in one workspace.
- **Best for:** Social Graphics, Image Editing, Design Mockups
- **Standout:** Generous free daily generations suit casual and frequent creators
- **Watch out for:** Free plan limits exports compared with paid subscription tiers
- **Pricing:** Freemium

---

## Productivity

The best of these remove a recurring task rather than adding a new tab. Research, note retrieval, task triage, document drafting — if it takes you out of your own workspace to be useful, it usually stops being useful within a month.

### 21. [[link:/tools/5|Notion AI]]
Notion AI is the built-in assistant for Notion workspaces, embedded directly in the docs, wikis, and databases teams already keep there.
- **Best for:** Summarize Docs, Answer Questions, Fill Properties
- **Standout:** Embedded in Notion, so no switching between apps is needed
- **Watch out for:** Only useful for teams already working inside Notion
- **Pricing:** Freemium

### 22. [[link:/tools/10|Perplexity AI]]
Perplexity is an AI-powered answer engine that responds to questions with cited, up-to-date information from the web.
- **Best for:** Research Answers, Fact Checking, Follow-Up Research
- **Standout:** Numbered citations make it easy to trace every answer to sources
- **Watch out for:** Answer quality depends on the sources it finds online
- **Pricing:** Freemium

### 23. [[link:/tools/14|Obsidian Copilot]]
[[link:/tools/245|Obsidian]] Copilot is a community plugin that brings AI assistance into Obsidian vaults.
- **Best for:** Chat With Vault, Note Commands, Connect Sources
- **Standout:** Answers can be grounded in your own notes rather than the web
- **Watch out for:** Requires setup with a model provider or local model to function
- **Pricing:** Freemium

### 24. [[link:/tools/52|ClickUp AI]]
ClickUp AI adds artificial intelligence features to the ClickUp project management platform.
- **Best for:** Sprint Planning, Meeting Follow-Up, Document Drafts
- **Standout:** AI features integrated directly into existing ClickUp workflows
- **Watch out for:** Most useful only for teams already using ClickUp
- **Pricing:** Freemium

### 25. [[link:/tools/54|AutoGPT]]
AutoGPT is an open-source experiment in autonomous AI agents.
- **Best for:** Agent Research, Task Automation, Learning Projects
- **Standout:** Fully open-source codebase maintained by an active community
- **Watch out for:** Research-stage tool; autonomous runs may need close supervision
- **Pricing:** Open Source

### 26. [[link:/tools/55|AgentGPT]]
AgentGPT is a browser-based autonomous agent.
- **Best for:** Research Delegation, Task Chaining, Exploratory Planning
- **Standout:** Runs entirely in the browser with no local installation
- **Pricing:** Freemium

### 27. [[link:/tools/56|CrewAI]]
CrewAI is an open-source Python framework for orchestrating role-based multi-agent systems.
- **Best for:** Multi-Agent Systems, Workflow Automation, Agent Debugging
- **Standout:** Open-source framework supported by an active developer community
- **Watch out for:** Requires solid Python development skills for effective use
- **Pricing:** Open Source

### 28. [[link:/tools/60|Harvey]]
Harvey is an AI assistant built specifically for legal work, aimed at law firms and in-house counsel rather than general office users.
- **Best for:** Contract Review, Due Diligence, Legal Research
- **Standout:** Purpose-built for legal workflows instead of generic office productivity tasks
- **Watch out for:** Enterprise licensing and deployment are aimed at firms, not individual lawyers
- **Pricing:** Paid

---

## Coding Assistants

Autocomplete got good first and matters most; whole-session agents got good later and matter more. The distinction that counts is scope: single-line suggestions inside the editor, or multi-file changes across a repository.

### 29. [[link:/tools/7|GitHub Copilot]]
GitHub Copilot is a widely used AI coding assistant that suggests code directly inside VS Code, JetBrains IDEs, Neovim, and other editors.
- **Best for:** Inline Suggestions, Test Drafting, Code Explanation
- **Standout:** Works across many popular editors and programming languages
- **Watch out for:** Requires a paid subscription for most individual users
- **Pricing:** Paid

### 30. [[link:/tools/13|Cursor]]
Cursor is an AI-first code editor built around pair programming with a model.
- **Best for:** Repo-wide Chat, Multi-file Edits, Rapid Prototyping
- **Standout:** AI features built into the editor, not bolted on
- **Watch out for:** Requires a paid plan for heavy AI usage
- **Pricing:** Freemium

### 31. [[link:/tools/17|Tabnine]]
Tabnine is an AI coding assistant offering code completion and chat inside popular IDEs.
- **Best for:** Local Completion, Private Assistants, Regulated Environments
- **Standout:** Can run fully locally or self-hosted on company servers
- **Watch out for:** Running locally requires more local compute than cloud-based assistants
- **Pricing:** Freemium

### 32. [[link:/tools/83|Codium AI]]
Now known as [[link:/tools/1454|Qodo]], this tool focuses on code quality rather than speed.
- **Best for:** Unit Test Generation, Code Review, PR Quality Gates
- **Standout:** Focuses on test coverage and correctness, not autocomplete
- **Watch out for:** Requires setup time to tune rules and thresholds
- **Pricing:** Freemium

### 33. [[link:/tools/233|CodeWhisperer]]
CodeWhisperer is Amazon's AI code assistant, built as a plugin for VS Code and JetBrains.
- **Best for:** AWS Development, Boilerplate Code, Security Scanning
- **Standout:** Deep integration with AWS services and SDK examples
- **Watch out for:** Suggestions are strongest when working inside AWS projects
- **Pricing:** Freemium

### 34. [[link:/tools/85|Replit AI]]
An AI pair programmer inside Replit's cloud IDE that scaffolds apps, explains code and deploys them without local setup.
- **Best for:** Quick Prototyping, Learning To Code, Deploying Projects
- **Standout:** No local setup; coding, explaining, and deploying happen in the browser
- **Watch out for:** Requires a reliable internet connection and a browser to work
- **Pricing:** Freemium

### 35. [[link:/tools/92|Hugging Face]]
The hub for open models and datasets: host and fine-tune models, run inference through an API, and publish demos as Spaces.
- **Best for:** Model Discovery, Fine-Tuning Models, Sharing Demos
- **Standout:** Large library of open models and datasets across many domains and languages
- **Pricing:** Freemium

### 36. [[link:/tools/93|LangChain]]
A framework for building LLM applications: retrieval, tool calling, and agent graphs, with LangSmith for tracing and evaluation.
- **Best for:** RAG Applications, Agent Workflows, LLM Evaluation
- **Standout:** Composable building blocks speed up prototypes of retrieval and agent applications
- **Watch out for:** Abstractions change often, so upgrades can break existing application code
- **Pricing:** Open Source

---

## Audio & Music

Two very different jobs live in this category: turning text into speech, and turning a description into music. Pricing models differ sharply, because speech is metered by character and music is metered by track or by licence.

### 37. [[link:/tools/8|ElevenLabs]]
ElevenLabs is an AI voice platform for generating lifelike speech and cloning voices.
- **Best for:** Audiobook Narration, Game Character Voices, Content Localization
- **Standout:** Voice quality and emotional range are among the best available today
- **Watch out for:** Free tier is limited; serious production requires a paid plan
- **Pricing:** Freemium

### 38. [[link:/tools/11|Whisper]]
Whisper is OpenAI's open-source speech-to-text model.
- **Best for:** Subtitle Generation, Meeting Transcripts, Custom Pipelines
- **Standout:** Free to run locally with no per-minute transcription fees
- **Watch out for:** Larger models need substantial GPU memory to run comfortably
- **Pricing:** Open Source

### 39. [[link:/tools/1397|Suno]]
AI music generation platform that creates complete songs with vocals and instruments from simple text prompts in seconds.
- **Best for:** Background Music, Songwriting Ideas, Jingles and Ads
- **Standout:** Generates complete songs with vocals in seconds from a text prompt
- **Watch out for:** Generated songs can sound generic without careful prompt refinement
- **Pricing:** Freemium

### 40. [[link:/tools/69|Soundraw]]
Soundraw generates royalty-free instrumental music from parameters like mood, genre and track length.
- **Best for:** Video Background Music, Podcast Beds, Section Editing
- **Standout:** Royalty-free license simplifies using music in published videos
- **Pricing:** Freemium

### 41. [[link:/tools/70|AIVA]]
AIVA is an AI music composer focused on classical and cinematic scoring.
- **Best for:** Film Scoring, Game Music, Background Tracks
- **Standout:** Style presets and parameters make classical composition accessible to non-musicians
- **Watch out for:** Outputs lean toward classical styles, with less strength in pop or hip-hop
- **Pricing:** Freemium

### 42. [[link:/tools/71|Beatoven]]
Beatoven is an AI music generator that creates background music matched to a video's mood and scene length.
- **Best for:** Video Scoring, YouTube Soundtracks, Ad Backgrounds
- **Standout:** Per-scene control lets music follow a video's changing moods
- **Pricing:** Freemium

### 43. [[link:/tools/78|Murf AI]]
Studio-quality AI voice generator with 120+ realistic voices across 20+ languages, used by 30,000+ teams at companies like Google, Meta, and Deloitte.
- **Best for:** Corporate Training Videos, Podcast Intros & Outros, E-Learning Narration
- **Standout:** 120+ voices with granular control over pitch, speed, pause, and emphasis — studio-grade output
- **Watch out for:** Free plan limited to 10 minutes of voice generation — not enough for serious projects
- **Pricing:** Freemium

### 44. [[link:/tools/79|Descript]]
Descript is an audio and video editor built around the transcript: editing the text cuts the audio.
- **Best for:** Podcast Editing, Video Narration, Screen Recordings
- **Standout:** Transcript-based editing makes audio work accessible to non-editors
- **Pricing:** Freemium

---

## Video Editing

Generation is the headline and captioning is the workhorse. If you already have footage, an editor with accurate subtitles will change your output more than a text-to-video model will — and cost less while doing it.

### 45. [[link:/tools/9|Runway ML]]
Runway ML is a browser-based suite for AI video generation and editing.
- **Best for:** Text-to-Video, Motion Brush, Video Inpainting
- **Standout:** Combines generation and editing tools on a single timeline
- **Watch out for:** The wide toolset comes with a real learning curve
- **Pricing:** Freemium

### 46. [[link:/tools/1465|Pika]]
Pika is an AI video generation platform that creates and edits videos from text prompts.
- **Best for:** Stylized Clips, Style Control, Social Video
- **Standout:** Style controls allow creative direction over generated output
- **Watch out for:** Artistic focus is less suited to realistic product video
- **Pricing:** Freemium

### 47. [[link:/tools/16|Sora]]
Sora is OpenAI's video generation model.
- **Best for:** Text to Video, Scene Continuity, Concept Footage
- **Standout:** Available inside ChatGPT, a platform many users already have
- **Watch out for:** Free tier limits generation volume and clip length
- **Pricing:** Freemium

### 48. [[link:/tools/51|VEED.io]]
Browser-based AI video editor used by 50M+ creators, with 100,000+ 5-star reviews.
- **Best for:** Social Media Reels, Course Video Editing, Multilingual Content
- **Standout:** No software to install — everything runs in the browser with automatic cloud saving
- **Watch out for:** Browser-based means performance depends on internet speed and browser capabilities
- **Pricing:** Freemium

### 49. [[link:/tools/80|Adobe Premiere Pro AI]]
Adobe Premiere Pro is a professional video editing application whose AI features assist with common editing tasks.
- **Best for:** Text-Based Editing, Social Reframing, Gap Filling
- **Standout:** AI tools integrate into an established professional editing workflow
- **Watch out for:** Requires a paid Adobe subscription, which is expensive long-term
- **Pricing:** Paid

### 50. [[link:/tools/81|HeyGen]]
HeyGen is an avatar video generation platform for marketing and training content.
- **Best for:** Avatar Marketing, Video Translation, Training Content
- **Standout:** Lip-synced avatars remove the need for on-camera presenters
- **Pricing:** Freemium

### 51. [[link:/tools/82|D-ID]]
D-ID creates talking-head videos from a single photo paired with a script or audio track.
- **Best for:** Talking-Head Videos, Streaming Avatars, Social Content
- **Standout:** Produces video from a single photo, no camera needed
- **Watch out for:** Output is mostly limited to head-and-shoulders talking formats
- **Pricing:** Freemium

### 52. [[link:/tools/96|Synthesia]]
The world's leading AI video avatar platform, trusted by 60,000+ businesses including 50% of Fortune 100 companies.
- **Best for:** Employee Onboarding Videos, Product Demo Videos, Personalized Sales Videos
- **Standout:** 160+ diverse AI avatars with natural expressions, gestures, and lip-sync accuracy
- **Watch out for:** Starting at $22/month, significantly more expensive than text-to-speech alternatives
- **Pricing:** Paid

### 53. [[link:/tools/98|Lovable]]
Generates full-stack web applications from a prompt, covering frontend, database, and auth, with code you can export and own.
- **Best for:** MVP Prototyping, Internal Tools, Learning Projects
- **Standout:** Generates frontend, database, and auth from a single natural-language prompt
- **Watch out for:** Complex or unusual requirements still need manual coding after generation
- **Pricing:** Freemium

### 54. [[link:/tools/201|Pictory]]
AI video repurposing tool that transforms long-form content — blog posts, webinars, podcasts — into viral short-form videos for social media in minutes.
- **Best for:** Blog-to-Video Content, Webinar Highlight Clips, YouTube Short Generation
- **Standout:** Unique blog-to-video and webinar-to-clip features — no other tool automates content repurposing this well
- **Watch out for:** Video output is limited to 1080p maximum — no 4K export option available
- **Pricing:** Freemium

---

## More Tools Worth Knowing

Another fourteen that did not fit the six categories above but keep earning a place in a stack. Same format, same rule: real vendor information, no rankings.

- [[link:/tools/1531|Wordtune]] — Wordtune is an AI writing companion that rewrites sentences for clarity, tone, and style. **Pricing:** Freemium.
- [[link:/tools/249|Anyword]] — Anyword is an AI copywriting platform built around predictive performance scores. **Pricing:** Paid.
- [[link:/tools/459|Recraft]] — Recraft is an AI design tool for creating and regenerating vector graphics and illustrations. **Pricing:** Freemium.
- [[link:/tools/1532|Clipdrop]] — Clipdrop is an AI-powered image editing suite with tools for background removal, relighting, cleanup and upscaling. **Pricing:** Freemium.
- [[link:/tools/1533|Photoroom]] — Photoroom is an AI photo tool that removes backgrounds and turns simple smartphone photos into studio-quality product images. **Pricing:** Freemium.
- [[link:/tools/1500|NotebookLM]] — NotebookLM is Google's research assistant that answers questions only from the sources you upload. **Pricing:** Freemium.
- [[link:/tools/1519|Granola]] — Granola is an AI notepad for meetings that transcribes in the background and merges the transcript with your own typed notes into a structured summary. **Pricing:** Freemium.
- [[link:/tools/1520|Fathom]] — Fathom is an AI meeting notetaker that records, transcribes and summarises Zoom, Google Meet and Teams calls, then drafts follow-up emails. **Pricing:** Freemium.
- [[link:/tools/1506|Dify]] — Dify is an open-source platform for building and shipping production AI applications. **Pricing:** Freemium.
- [[link:/tools/1505|n8n]] — n8n is a workflow automation platform for connecting apps and building agentic automations. **Pricing:** Freemium.
- [[link:/tools/1521|AssemblyAI]] — AssemblyAI is a speech-to-text API built for developers who need transcription plus structured understanding of audio. **Pricing:** Freemium.
- [[link:/tools/1512|CapCut]] — CapCut is ByteDance's video editor, widely used for producing TikTok videos, Instagram Reels, and YouTube Shorts. **Pricing:** Freemium.
- [[link:/tools/1513|Vidu]] — Vidu is a text- and image-to-video model from ShengShu Technology. **Pricing:** Freemium.
- [[link:/tools/1474|Kapwing]] — Kapwing is a browser-based video editor with AI features for captioning, translation, and content repurposing. **Pricing:** Freemium.

## Getting Started Without Buying Six Subscriptions

1. **Write the task down first.** One sentence naming the job and the constraint. If no tool on this list matches it, the problem is not a tool problem.
2. **Start on free tiers.** Every tool here that has a free plan lets you reach a real verdict before paying; the ones that do not are marked Paid.
3. **Learn one, then add the next.** Most people who switch tools three times a month would have been better served learning the first one properly.
4. **Re-check pricing quarterly.** Tiers move, and a tool that was too expensive in March is often competitive by September.

## Final Thoughts

The fifty-four above cover the work most people need an AI tool for. None of them replace judgement about what to make, and none of them are worth a subscription you are not using monthly. Pick the one tool that removes your worst recurring task, use it until it is boring, then add the next.

**Ready to look around?** Browse the [full directory](/) or read the [blog](/blog) for longer comparisons.
tldr: 54 AI tools grouped by what you actually do — writing, images, productivity, coding, audio and video — each with pricing, real use cases, the one thing it does best, and the catch.
